content.json:
# L3 Triage Dashboard
Incident KPIs, severity distribution, top firing detections, ATT&CK tactic spread, entity hotspots, MTTA/MTTR, closure classification, tuning candidates, SLA breaches and the open queue.

*Author: Sandeep Mothukuri — part of [sentinel-detection-engine](https://github.com/sandeepmothukuri/sentinel-detection-engine)*

> Every panel is computed from `SecurityIncident` / `SecurityAlert` in the workspace this workbook is deployed to. Nothing here is sample data: on a workspace with no incidents the tiles render empty, which is the correct answer, not a fault.

> **Closure discipline note.** The closure-classification and tuning panels read the `Classification` column. An incident that was never triaged shows as Undetermined and is *not* counted as a false positive — precision figures are only meaningful once analysts close incidents properly.

content.title: Incident KPIs (latest state per incident)

content.query:
SecurityIncident
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by IncidentNumber
| summarize Incidents = count() by Severity
| order by Severity asc
content.title: Incidents by severity (latest state)

content.query:
SecurityAlert
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| summarize Alerts = count() by AlertName
| top 10 by Alerts desc
content.title: Top 10 firing detections (alert volume)
Detection trend — alert volume per day by severity

content.query:
SecurityAlert
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| mv-expand Tactic = todynamic(Tactics)
| extend Tactic = tostring(Tactic)
| where isnotempty(Tactic)
| summarize Alerts = count() by Tactic
| order by Alerts desc
content.title: Alerts per MITRE ATT&CK tactic

content.query:
// Entities is a string column on SecurityAlert that carries a JSON array.
SecurityAlert
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| extend Entities = parse_json(Entities)
| mv-expand e = Entities
| extend Type = tostring(e.Type)
| extend Value = coalesce(tostring(e.Name), tostring(e.Address), tostring(e.HostName), tostring(e.UPNSuffix), tostring(e.FullName))
| where isnotempty(Value)
| summarize Hits = count() by Type, Value
| top 20 by Hits desc
content.title: Top entities (accounts, hosts, IPs)

content.query:
// MTTA = first modification - creation. FirstModifiedTime is the platform's
// first-touch timestamp; FirstActivityTime is when the *underlying event*
// happened, which measures detection latency instead (see the latency panel).
// MTTR is only defined for closed incidents, so it ignores null ClosedTime rows.
SecurityIncident
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by IncidentNumber
| extend MTTA_min = datetime_diff('minute', FirstModifiedTime, CreatedTime)
| extend MTTR_min = iff(Status =~ 'Closed', datetime_diff('minute', ClosedTime, CreatedTime), int(null))
| summarize
    Incidents = count(),
    ['MTTA avg (min)'] = round(avg(MTTA_min), 1),
    ['MTTA p95 (min)'] = percentile(MTTA_min, 95),
    ['MTTR avg (min)'] = round(avg(MTTR_min), 1),
    ['MTTR p95 (min)'] = percentile(MTTR_min, 95)
    by Severity
| order by Severity asc
content.title: MTTA / MTTR by severity (minutes)

content.query:
// Detection latency: alert time minus the time the underlying event occurred.
// This is a property of the rule schedule and ingestion pipeline, not of the
// analyst — compare it against each rule's queryFrequency.
SecurityAlert
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| extend LatencyMin = datetime_diff('minute', TimeGenerated, StartTime)
| where LatencyMin >= 0
| summarize
    Alerts = count(),
    ['p50 (min)'] = percentile(LatencyMin, 50),
    ['p95 (min)'] = percentile(LatencyMin, 95),
    ['max (min)'] = max(LatencyMin)
    by AlertName
| top 15 by Alerts desc
content.title: Detection latency by rule (event time → alert time)
Closed incidents by classification
Tuning candidates — rules with a false-positive rate of 30% or more (minimum 5 closures)

content.query:
// SLA breaches. Targets come from docs/workflows/escalation-matrix.md:
// High acknowledged (first modified) within 5 minutes, Medium within 60.
// Only open incidents can be in breach — closed ones are measured by MTTA above.
let high_target_min = 5;
let medium_target_min = 60;
SecurityIncident
| where TimeGenerated {TimeRange}
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by IncidentNumber
| where Status in~ ('New', 'Active')
| extend AgeMin = datetime_diff('minute', now(), CreatedTime)
| extend AckMin = iff(isnotnull(FirstModifiedTime), datetime_diff('minute', FirstModifiedTime, CreatedTime), int(null))
| extend TargetMin = case(
      Severity =~ 'High', high_target_min,
      Severity =~ 'Medium', medium_target_min,
      int(null))
| where isnotnull(TargetMin)
| extend ['Unacknowledged past target'] = isnull(AckMin) and AgeMin > TargetMin
| extend ['Acknowledged late'] = isnotnull(AckMin) and AckMin > TargetMin
| where ['Unacknowledged past target'] or ['Acknowledged late']
| project IncidentNumber, Title, Severity, Status,
          Owner = tostring(Owner.userPrincipalName),
          ['Age (min)'] = AgeMin, ['Ack (min)'] = AckMin, ['Target (min)'] = TargetMin,
          CreatedTime
| order by ['Age (min)'] desc
content.title: SLA breaches in the open queue (High > 5 min, Medium > 60 min)

content.query:
// Telemetry freshness. `union isfuzzy=true` means a table from a connector you
// have not enabled yet contributes nothing instead of failing the whole panel —
// so this tile is safe to read on a partially deployed workspace, where the
// missing sources simply have no row. A source whose last event is hours old is
// an ingestion problem the detections depend on, not an analyst problem.
union isfuzzy=true withsource=SourceTable
    (SigninLogs | project TimeGenerated),
    (AuditLogs | project TimeGenerated),
    (OfficeActivity | project TimeGenerated),
    (AzureActivity | project TimeGenerated),
    (DeviceProcessEvents | project TimeGenerated),
    (DeviceNetworkEvents | project TimeGenerated),
    (DeviceFileEvents | project TimeGenerated),
    (AzureDiagnostics | project TimeGenerated)
| summarize
    ['Last event (UTC)'] = max(TimeGenerated),
    ['Events in range'] = count(),
    ['Age (hours)'] = round(datetime_diff('minute', now(), max(TimeGenerated)) / 60.0, 1)
    by SourceTable
| order by ['Age (hours)'] asc
content.title: Telemetry freshness by source (safe on partially deployed workspaces)
Open incidents (latest state)

content.json:
---

### Reading this dashboard

| Panel | What it answers |
|---|---|
| Incident KPIs | Is the queue growing, and is anything sitting unassigned? |
| Incidents by severity | Where the analyst time is going |
| Top firing detections | Which rules drive volume (cross-check against `expectedVolume` in the rule metadata) |
| Detection trend | A step change in one severity band is usually a rule or connector change |
| Alerts per tactic | Whether the estate is being probed in one ATT&CK phase |
| Top entities | Repeat-offender accounts, hosts and IPs |
| MTTA / MTTR | Triage and resolution performance against the escalation matrix |
| Detection latency | Whether a rule is meeting its own `queryFrequency` promise |
| Closure classification | Analyst agreement with the alerts — the input to tuning |
| Tuning candidates | Rules to work through the tuning loop |
| SLA breaches | Incidents that missed their acknowledgement target |
| Telemetry freshness | Whether the connectors the detections depend on are still feeding |

The tuning thresholds on this page (5 closed incidents, 30% FP rate) are the same ones documented in
[`tests/validation/performance-metrics.md`](https://github.com/sandeepmothukuri/sentinel-detection-engine/blob/main/tests/validation/performance-metrics.md)
and in the tuning loop in [`docs/tuning.md`](https://github.com/sandeepmothukuri/sentinel-detection-engine/blob/main/docs/tuning.md).
Changing one without the other is a documentation defect.
